title: Formula audit: fix five broken sheets

docs.syntax: each error code names one break: a zero divisor, a missing key, text in arithmetic, a wrong range, a misspelling
docs.explain: This capstone is the reverse of everything before it. The other lessons hand you a question and ask for a formula; here the formula exists, it is broken, and the sheet shows you the error code it broke with. Reading that code is the skill. A division error means the denominator can be zero, and the fix is a guard rather than a different function. A not-available error means a lookup found nothing, and the fix is to test for the row before asking for it. A value error means one of the operands is text and the arithmetic has no number to work with, which is caught with a type test. A reference error means a range points outside the data, and the fix is to read the range against the table rather than to trust the mouse. A name error means the function was mistyped, and the repair is spelling. The five screens here are one of each, in that order, and each one takes a different function to repair, which is why the audit is the last lesson in the track rather than an early one.

errors.text: A denominator is zero, so the division has no result.
A lookup key is not in the table, so there is no row to read.
An operand is text where a number is needed.
A range points outside the data, so it no longer exists.
A function name is misspelled, so the sheet does not know it.

docs.atWork: Opening a workbook someone else built and fixing it from the error code down.
docs.outcome: Repair five broken cells, one per error code, by choosing the test each code implies.
docs.teaches: an error-code-first repair: guard, key test, type test, range, spelling
docs.dataset: Five broken sheets, one per error code, to repair in place

screens.prompt: In D3, repair the ratio for the rep with no visits so it reads n/a instead of an error.

hints.func-if: The cell has to choose between a word and a division.
hints.require-ref: The visits figure for that rep is in B3.
hints.value: With no visits the answer is the word n/a, not a number.
hints.error: A zero divisor is exactly what the guard is there to catch.

reject.why: the division is left to break on a zero denominator
the error is swallowed rather than tested for
the repair reads the wrong word
a trailing space is added to the repaired word
the guard is written against the first rep rather than the broken row
the guard tests the wrong thing, so the zero divisor is still reached
the arguments fall outside the parentheses

screens.prompt: In F2, repair the lookup so a name that is not in the list reads not found instead of an error.

hints.syntax: =IF(COUNTIF(A2:A5,E2)=0,"not found",VLOOKUP(E2,A2:C5,3,FALSE)) — count the key first, then look it up.
hints.func-countif: The key is tested for before the lookup asks for its row.
hints.func-vlookup: The orders figure is read from the third column of the rep table.
hints.require-ref: The typed name is in E2.
hints.value: Zed is not in the list, so the answer is the word not found.
hints.error: A lookup of a missing key is what returns #N/A, so the test must come first.

reject.why: the lookup is left to fail on a missing key, with no test in front of it
the repair types the words with a space in front of them
the repair reads the wrong words
the test is the wrong way round, so the lookup still runs on a missing key
the real row is never looked up, so every present rep reads found
the key is never tested against the list
the typed name is hard-coded instead of read from its cell
the test itself divides by zero
the arguments fall outside the parentheses

screens.prompt: In D3, repair the line value so a quantity that is not a number contributes nothing instead of failing.

hints.syntax: =IF(ISNUMBER(B3),B3*C3,0) — test the operand's type, then multiply.
hints.func-isnumber: The quantity is text on that row, so the fix starts with a type test.
hints.value: A line with no usable quantity is worth nothing, so it contributes zero.
hints.error: Multiplying text by a price is what raises the value error.

reject.why: the multiplication is left to fail on a text quantity
the zero is typed rather than decided by the quantity
an empty string is not the zero the line is worth
a line with no quantity is counted as one unit
the test is applied to the price, so the text quantity is still multiplied
the guard is written against the first line rather than the broken row
the repaired value is then divided by zero
the arguments fall outside the parentheses

screens.prompt: In D2, repair the North total so its ranges cover every row of the table.

hints.syntax: =SUMIF(A2:A5,"North",B2:B5) — the labels, the criterion, then the amounts.
hints.func-sumif: Only the North rows count, so the total needs a criterion.
hints.value: A hundred and a hundred and fifty are the two North rows, so 250.
hints.error: A range that points outside the table is what raised the reference error.

reject.why: every region is added rather than the North rows
the ranges stop before the second North row
the South row is totalled instead
the first row is left out of both ranges
the total is then divided by zero
the arguments fall outside the parentheses

screens.prompt: In D2, repair the average so it stops reading a name error and reports the score column.

hints.syntax: =AVERAGE(B2:B5) — the function name, then the score column.
hints.func-average: The repaired cell reports the mean of the scores.
hints.error: A misspelled function name is what raised the name error.

reject.why: the name is still misspelled
the scores are added rather than averaged
the last score is outside the range
the first score is outside the range
the average is then divided by zero
the argument falls outside the parentheses
